Subject: Audit-log & retention playbook — evidence handoff and SOC 2 asks

Hi Javier / Ava —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can keep momentum with your security team and the procurement timeline.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Primary concern: retention and tamper-evidence for audit logs across tokenized PII and transactional events.
- Scope: SOC 2 Type II coverage required for production APIs and logging infrastructure, plus DPA terms for Log retention and deletion notices.
- Short-term ask: sample redacted audit logs and a pen-test attestation to map to our acceptance checklist.
- Timeline: your procurement team is hoping to complete security review by the end of May.

Concrete next steps (asks from FinSecure to Redwood)
1) We will share a SOC 2 report (redacted) and the pen-test summary/attestation you mentioned. Please send via secure link or SFTP.
2) Please provide an export of a redacted audit_log sample (events for a single merchant day) so we can validate fields and retention lifecycle.
3) We will fill the attached Redwood SOC 2 mapping template and return with notes.
4) Confirm retention options: 90 days default / 7 years archival option / retention exceptions process. Need confirmation whether logs can be exported with HMAC or other integrity markers.

Attachments I will upload to the shared secure folder after this note:
- redwood-soc2-gap-mapping-template.xlsx (Request: fill by Thu 2028-05-12)

Proposed deadlines
- May 12: FinSecure returns filled mapping template and any open questions
- May 15: Redwood ingests sample log and confirms retention mapping and integrity approach
- May 22: Final evidence handoff (SOC2 + pen test + DPA redlines)

If that works, I’ll follow up with a short calendar invite that covers an artifacts handoff working session (30 min).

Thanks — Kim

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear summary. Confirming a few items from our side:
- We can share a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and a one‑page pen-test attestation (no PII in docs). Attaching the pen-test summary draft (we will finalize next week).
- Sample logs: we can provide one day of events from our staging environment (redacted). Format will be ndjson, timestamps in UTC, will include event_id, user_hash, action, resource_type, ip_country, and integrity_signature (HMAC-SHA256).
- Retention: our compliance team prefers 1 year hot retention, 7 years cold archival for transaction metadata. We do have a pending question on legal holds — can Redwood support export-on-demand for legal holds within 48 hours?

We'll upload the two items (pen-test summary + sample ndjson) to the secure S3 link by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,

Thanks Javier — helpful. A couple quick notes from the ops side:

- Export-on-demand for legal holds: yes, Redwood supports on-demand retention exports. We can deliver a signed export package (ndjson + manifest + signatures) within 48 hours for critical holds; for standard exports the SLA is 72 hours.
- Integrity markers: our runtime can support HMAC-SHA256 signatures on every log line and we keep a tamper-evident chain for the KV used to store signatures.
- We’ll take the sample ndjson and run a short validation script against it to confirm field mappings and timestamp ordering.

Action items we own: 
1) Ben: validate provided ndjson sample and return file-level validation notes (due 2028-05-15).
2) Irene: prepare a short write-up on our archival options and the DPA language that maps to retention/exports (due 2028-05-17).
